page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The system is equipped with 188.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 3.91 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates under a QEMU hypervisor. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests placing the instance in the top 25% of its class. The dedicated AMD EPYC processor delivers strong performance in database operations, cryptography, and Redis SET operations, which reached 64.55 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, with uncached write speeds performing in the top 25% at 95.71 GB/sec. Software compilation with Clang and ray tracing benchmarks also demonstrate strong performance, while static web serving throughput and medium-to-large LLM inference speeds remain in the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx63 offers a high density of dedicated physical cores and bundled NVMe storage, making it a resource-dense option for workloads requiring sustained CPU performance without the virtualization overhead of shared-core instances. The primary tradeoff is the balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio of roughly 1:4, which may limit its suitability for memory-intensive in-memory databases that require a higher RAM-to-CPU ratio.

This hardware profile is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, database hosting, Redis caching layers, and general-purpose enterprise applications. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable performance, making it appropriate for production environments, CI/CD runners, and moderate-scale web serving.
